precepts.text: Nebuchadnezzar made an image of gold and decreed that whoever fell not down and worshipped it should be cast into the burning fiery furnace.
precepts.point: Daniel told him he would be driven from men to eat grass until he knew the Most High ruleth in the kingdom of men. Twelve months later he said, Is not this great Babylon that I have built by the might of my power? While the word was in his mouth, the kingdom departed from him. He humbled himself and confessed there is no God like Daniel's God.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
Nebuchadnezzar is the head of gold in Daniel's dream, and before God humbled him in chapter 4, his pride is shown in chapter 3: “Nebuchadnezzar the king made an image of gold, whose height was threescore cubits, and the breadth thereof six cubits: he set it up in the plain of Dura, in the province of Babylon.” In his pride he set up a golden image and said everybody should worship it.

He gathered the princes, the governors, the captains, the judges and all the rulers of the provinces to its dedication, and “an herald cried aloud, To you it is commanded, O people, nations, and languages”, that when they heard the music they should “fall down and worship the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king hath set up”. And “whoso falleth not down and worshippeth shall the same hour be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace.”

That is the same thing America does now with the flag. You don't bow down to it; now you have to stand up and salute it and honor it. It is the same as it was in ancient Babylon, just a different way.

This is why the decree of Daniel 4 came upon him. Nebuchadnezzar got prideful, and pride brings a man low. Twelve months after Daniel's interpretation he said, “Is not this great Babylon, that I have built for the house of the kingdom by the might of my power, and for the honour of my majesty?” God calls America Babylon the great, and Nebuchadnezzar called Babylon great himself. “While the word was in the king’s mouth”, the kingdom departed from him. You try to make people worship you, and it is taken.

He was made to eat grass as oxen “until thou know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men”. Until you humble yourself, you are eating grass. And he did humble himself; he came back and confessed there is no God like the God of Daniel. All kingdoms fall because of pride, Assyria, Babylon, the Greeks, Rome and America, and nobody is exempt from God's judgment for it.

precepts.point: Your vote does not choose the ruler. God sets the base men over Israel so they see what it means to want another nation to rule them.

note.label: Latinos For Trump: Alien Vs. Predator

precepts.why:
“the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will, and setteth up over it the basest of men.” It does not matter who you vote for; he puts whoever he wants. Donald Trump is one of the basest of men, a caricature and TV personality from The Apprentice, just as Ronald Reagan was an actor. His orange skin is telling you what he is about: he is Esau, the red man. The Most High puts these men over us so we can see: you wanted the other nations to rule over you besides me, and this is what happens.

Deuteronomy 17:14 shows that desire in our people: “When thou art come unto the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee, and shalt possess it, and shalt dwell therein, and shalt say, I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me”. We are not satisfied with the King of kings and Lord of lords, Christ, being over us. We always want to be like the other nations. That is why we dye our hair blonde, put in the contacts, put on the suit and tie, go to their universities and get their education, and assimilate to their way of life.

But the law says “Thou shalt in any wise set him king over thee, whom the Lord thy God shall choose: one from among thy brethren shalt thou set king over thee: thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother.” We have to have a king of our own people, who is for our people, not a base man out for the interest of corporations that rob and steal our resources. We are not supposed to vote for other nations to be over us. Thus saith the Lord.

The same goes for our people in Latin America. In Mexico and in Argentina, where an Italian was set up, what are they doing for you? Nothing, not a damn thing. You cannot set up people of other nations over you. That is why the Most High sets the basest of men over Israel: to show us what it means to choose a stranger over the king he chose.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
“The king’s heart is in the hand of the Lord, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.” The king in this nation right now, in 2026, is Donald Trump. His heart is in the hand of the Lord, and whatever way the Lord wants him to go, he is going to go, and he is going to fulfill what the Lord has in store.

Daniel shows why: “This matter is by the decree of the watchers, and the demand by the word of the holy ones: to the intent that the living may know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men.” God rules in the kingdoms of men. God is the ultimate ruler.

And what does he do? He “giveth it to whomsoever he will, and setteth up over it the basest of men.” He gives the kingdom over to whomever he chooses, and he sets over it the basest of men: the least of men, the bottom feeders. The bottom feeders are ruling us right now. Biden, Trump, Putin, all of them: they are the bottom.

So the king’s heart turning like rivers of water and the Most High setting up the basest of men are the same truth. Trump is not ruling by his own power. He is set up by the Most High and turned whithersoever he will, a sword in the hand of God to bring judgment on the nations.

note.label: War of the Gods

precepts.why:
Christ is “the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature,” because we have not seen the Most High’s face nor His shape nor heard His voice. The Most High created Christ, and Christ created everything else: “whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him.” For him means to do his will, for his glory. The nations are his sword, doing the Lord’s bidding by whipping Israel back to repentance.

Daniel shows who rules those thrones: “This matter is by the decree of the watchers, and the demand by the word of the holy ones: to the intent that the living may know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men.” There are kingdoms of men on every continent, in every country, town and village, but the Most High is ruling them.

“And giveth it to whomsoever he will.” The Lord determines who is that principality, who is that throne, who is that power. Christ is like a chess player moving all the pieces into place so that his will is done.

“And setteth up over it the basest of men”: the lowest of the low. You have to be low down to do what these nations have done to each other and to the nation of Israel. But we transgressed against the Lord, and He said, I have to teach you war. If all the powers were the nicest people on earth, there would be no war and no oppression, and nothing to learn. We have to fight to get back to where we are supposed to be. Brothers and sisters who send messages saying they are taking a break from IUIC are taking a break from the Lord, and that is not going to work.

note.label: America Hedgemony & Oppression

precepts.why:
Daniel says “the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will”, and Solomon shows how: “The king’s heart is in the hand of the Lord, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.” God turns the king's heart wherever he will. Whatever the Lord wants the king to do, he is going to do it.

So even in these last days, God gave who is ruling the world today. America is the superpower, and God put Trump in that position. Everything you see Trump doing today, God is allowing it. He is snatching people up off the street and sending them to prisons in other countries, and that is not outside the hand of the Most High.

This answers the question our people ask: why is God allowing Trump to do the things being done on the earth? Because the heart of that king is in the Lord's hand, and the Most High is setting up over the kingdom of men whom he will, even “the basest of men”, to bring his judgment to pass.

note.label: America Hedgemony & Oppression

precepts.why:
Why is God allowing Trump to do what he is doing? David answers it: “Arise, O Lord, disappoint him, cast him down: deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword”. The wicked is God's sword. The so-called white man is God's sword.

So when the Most High sets up “the basest of men” over the kingdom of men, he is taking up his sword. The wicked are not ruling on their own power; they are the weapon in God's hand, the same way the king's heart is in the hand of the Lord.

And the prayer shows what the righteous do while that sword is out: cry to the Lord to deliver our souls from the wicked. The sword is being used for judgment on the earth, and only the Lord can deliver his people from it.

note.label: America Hedgemony & Oppression

precepts.why:
“He made many to fall, yea, one fell upon another: and they said, Arise, and let us go again to our own people, and to the land of our nativity, from the oppressing sword.” The oppressing sword is the wicked, the sword of Psalms 17:13. And an oppressing sword is being risen up all over the earth, especially on the western hemisphere, and especially amongst our people.

Everything you see taking place with ICE, with how America went into Venezuela and snatched up its president, Trump telling the leader in Colombia he is next: that is the oppressing sword. We are living in the beginning of sorrows. It is going to get worse and worse, beyond the worst things you could think of. You thought World War II was bad; wait till you see what is about to happen on this earth. Don't sit back and be comfortable because nothing has happened to you yet.

God is using America, that administration, as his sword to bring judgment on the earth. It is the wine cup of Jeremiah 25:15: “Take the wine cup of this fury at my hand, and cause all the nations, to whom I send thee, to drink it.” And Jeremiah 51:7 shows whose hand that cup is in: “Babylon hath been a golden cup in the Lord’s hand, that made all the earth drunken: the nations have drunken of her wine; therefore the nations are mad.” Babylon is not just ancient Babylon; it is America. What is in that cup is falsehood, lies, oppression and ill dealing, and that is why the nations are becoming angry with America.

So under that oppressing sword, many fall, and the cry goes up: “let us go again to our own people, and to the land of our nativity”. This is why Daniel 4:17 matters now: the Most High rules in the kingdom of men, he has raised up the wicked as his sword over this side of the world where Israel is, and he is using it to bring judgment on the earth.

They are not chosen from among our brethren; God put them in position to check us, because some of our people were evil as hell.

Yet our people take the base men and women set up in this time for their leaders. Officer Tatum speaks of people that he loves and respects, people chosen by God, and he is not talking about black people; he is talking about the so-called Jews, Amalek, while they kill Palestinians and children by the tens of thousands, the same people who killed Martin Luther King, Malcolm X and the African leaders. These negroes forgot they did not come here voluntarily; they forgot the slave ships, the shackles, and the millions of forefathers who died. She is rebranding herself as a faithful Christian by going with the Republicans, but Republican or Democrat, it is the same beast.

Stop thinking you have a magic scripture for some of these negroes; some are our fathers, mothers, brothers and children, and their fate is sealed. They can only repent or die. The king over Israel must be one God chooses from among our brethren; everything else set over us now is the basest of men, and it is only for a time.

note.label: Exodus 18: Jethro's Counsel and Righteous Leadership

precepts.why:
Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, came to the same confession: “Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, all whose works are truth, and his ways judgment: and those that walk in pride he is able to abase.”

That is exactly what Jethro saw in Egypt: “in the thing wherein they dealt proudly he was above them.” The Egyptians walked in pride and the Lord abased them, and Nebuchadnezzar learned that those that walk in pride he is able to abase.

Jethro, Naaman and Nebuchadnezzar: the heathen understand that the Most High is greater than all other gods. It is our people that want a god that does not look like them.

precepts.why:
“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” The whole creation is waiting for the sons of God to be manifested. The great tree that fed and sheltered all flesh was hewn down by the decree of the watchers, its stump bound with iron and brass and a beast's heart given to him till seven times passed over him, “to the intent that the living may know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will, and setteth up over it the basest of men.”

That is what we see today: the basest of men ruling the earth. The Most High gave them the kingdom, the way he gave it to Nebuchadnezzar, and the way he took it from him.

The nations are waiting for us to wake up, shake off our sins, and take our place as the kings and priests of the earth. The kingdom of men sits in the hands of the basest until the sons of God are manifested; the earnest expectation of the creature is for that day.

note.label: Daniel 4: Nebuchadnezzar Abased Until He Knew the Most High Rules

precepts.why:
“All nations before him are as nothing; and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity.” Isaiah says of the nations what Nebuchadnezzar came to say of himself: “all the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing”. The greatest king on the earth in his day, with all Babylon under him, was less than nothing and vanity before the Most High, and it took until the end of the days, when his understanding returned, for him to understand it.

Then he blessed the Most High, “whose dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom is from generation to generation”. Kingdoms of men rise and fall; his does not. “he doeth according to his will in the army of heaven, and among the inhabitants of the earth: and none can stay his hand, or say unto him, What doest thou?” When the Most High declares a thing shall come to pass, it comes to pass, and no nation, counted less than nothing, can stay his hand.

note.label: Daniel 4: Nebuchadnezzar Abased Until He Knew the Most High Rules

precepts.why:
“The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up.” That is what happened to Nebuchadnezzar. The Most High brought him low, jacked him up, literally turned him to crawl like a bird with the heart of a beast; then he lifted him up again. His reason returned, and “for the glory of my kingdom, mine honour and brightness returned unto me”; his counsellors and his lords sought unto him, and excellent majesty was added unto him.

We already understood that the Most High can bring one up and set another down. But the heathen had to learn it by being jacked up. As soon as his understanding returned he praised the one true living God: “Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, all whose works are truth, and his ways judgment: and those that walk in pride he is able to abase.” Rich or poor, high or low, it is in the hand of the Lord, and pride is what he abases.
